title: Exponential Domain and Range
student_objective: I can determine and represent the domain and range of exponential functions in the form f(x)=abˣ.
teacher_objective: Diagnose confusion among domain, range, asymptote, initial value, sign, transformations, interval notation, discrete context, and graph behavior.

concept_cards.title: All real inputs work
concept_cards.content: For f(x)=abˣ with a≠0, every real x produces a value, so the mathematical domain is all real numbers.

concept_cards.title: The sign of a sets the range side
concept_cards.content: Because bˣ is always positive when b>0 and b≠1, a positive a gives outputs above 0 and a negative a gives outputs below 0.

concept_cards.title: Zero is the horizontal asymptote
concept_cards.content: For unshifted f(x)=abˣ, the graph approaches but never reaches y=0. Therefore 0 is excluded from the range.

concept_cards.title: Vertical shifts move the range
concept_cards.content: For f(x)=abˣ+k, the asymptote becomes y=k. If a>0, the range is y>k; if a<0, the range is y<k.

concept_cards.title: Context can restrict inputs
concept_cards.content: The parent function has all-real domain, but time, item counts, or other real situations may require nonnegative, whole-number, or bounded inputs.

items.prompt: State the domain of f(x)=2ˣ.
items.tutor_behavior: Exponential functions accept negative, zero, and positive real inputs.

items.prompt: Is 2ˣ ever equal to 0? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Connect positive exponential outputs to the horizontal asymptote y=0.

items.prompt: For f(x)=3(2ˣ), identify f(0).
items.tutor_behavior: Use b⁰=1, so f(0)=a.

items.prompt: Determine the domain and range of f(x)=4(3ˣ).
items.answer_key: domain: all real numbers; range: y > 0
accepted_answers: domain all real numbers range y>0

solution_steps.explanation: The graph approaches but does not reach 0.

items.tutor_behavior: Separate the horizontal input set from the positive output set.

items.prompt: Determine the domain and range of g(x)=-2(5ˣ).
items.answer_key: domain: all real numbers; range: y < 0
accepted_answers: domain all real numbers range y<0

solution_steps.explanation: The negative coefficient does not restrict x.
A negative coefficient reflects positive outputs below the x-axis.

items.tutor_behavior: Do not reverse domain and range after reflection.

items.prompt: Determine the range of h(x)=2ˣ+6.

solution_steps.explanation: The positive graph stays above its asymptote.

items.tutor_behavior: Move the asymptote and preserve the strict inequality.

items.prompt: State the range of f(x)=7(0.5ˣ).
items.tutor_behavior: Decay changes direction across x, not the positive side of the range.

items.prompt: State the range of f(x)=-3(2ˣ)+4.
items.tutor_behavior: The negative coefficient puts outputs below the shifted asymptote y=4.

items.prompt: A savings model uses t≥0. State its contextual domain.
items.tutor_behavior: Use the stated time restriction instead of the parent-function domain.

items.prompt: State the domain of f(x)=-5(4ˣ).
items.tutor_behavior: Output reflection does not restrict inputs.

items.prompt: State the range of f(x)=6(3ˣ)-2.
items.tutor_behavior: The graph stays above the asymptote y=-2.

items.prompt: Write the range y<5 in interval notation.
items.tutor_behavior: Use a parenthesis at 5 because the endpoint is excluded.

items.prompt: A bacteria count is measured only at whole hours 0 through 12. State the contextual domain.
items.tutor_behavior: Combine the interval restriction with discrete whole-hour inputs.

items.prompt: State the domain of f(x)=9(2ˣ).
items.tutor_behavior: All real exponents are valid.

items.prompt: State the range of f(x)=-4(3ˣ).
items.tutor_behavior: The reflected graph stays below but never reaches zero.

items.prompt: State the range of f(x)=2(5ˣ)+7.
items.tutor_behavior: Use the shifted asymptote y=7 and positive coefficient.

items.prompt: State the range of f(x)=-6(0.2ˣ)-3.
items.tutor_behavior: Base size affects growth or decay, while sign and shift set the range side.

items.prompt: A student says the range of f(x)=3(2ˣ) is y≥0 because the graph approaches 0. Write the correct range.
items.explanation_guidance: The exponential output is always positive and approaches the horizontal asymptote y=0 without reaching it.
items.tutor_behavior: Require the distinction between approaching an asymptote and including an endpoint.

items.prompt: What is the horizontal asymptote of f(x)=5ˣ?
items.tutor_behavior: Use the unshifted exponential parent asymptote.

items.prompt: For f(x)=8(3ˣ), is every output positive? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Both 8 and 3ˣ are positive.

items.prompt: What is the horizontal asymptote of f(x)=2ˣ-9?
items.tutor_behavior: Shift y=0 down 9 units.

items.prompt: State the range of f(x)=-2ˣ+8.
items.tutor_behavior: Interpret -2ˣ as -(2ˣ), then shift up 8.

items.prompt: Write all real numbers in interval notation.
items.tutor_behavior: Infinity symbols always use parentheses.

items.prompt: Does changing the base from 2 to 0.5 change the domain? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Both valid positive bases accept every real exponent.

items.prompt: State the range of f(x)=-0.5(4ˣ)+12.
items.tutor_behavior: The negative coefficient keeps outputs below the asymptote y=12.

items.prompt: A graph has horizontal asymptote y=5 and lies entirely above it. State its range.
items.tutor_behavior: Translate the graph position and excluded asymptote into a strict inequality.

items.prompt: A graph has horizontal asymptote y=-4 and lies entirely below it. State its range.
items.tutor_behavior: Use outputs below the excluded boundary.

items.prompt: A student claims f(x)=2ˣ has domain x>0 because outputs are positive. Name the confusion.
items.tutor_behavior: Inputs are all real; positivity describes outputs.

items.prompt: A medication model starts at t=0 and is used for the next 24 hours. State its contextual domain.
items.tutor_behavior: Use the meaningful time interval supplied by the situation.

items.prompt: For f(x)=abˣ+k with a>0, state the range in terms of k.
items.tutor_behavior: A positive multiple stays above the shifted asymptote y=k.

domain_all_reals.teacher_signal: Restricts the mathematical domain without cause

zero_exclusion.teacher_signal: Includes the horizontal asymptote in the range

negative_range.teacher_signal: Does not reflect the output range

vertical_shift_range.teacher_signal: Does not shift the asymptote and range boundary

reflection_shift_range.teacher_signal: Uses the wrong side of a shifted asymptote

discrete_domain.teacher_signal: Treats discrete contextual inputs as continuous

growth_decay_domain.teacher_signal: Believes growth or decay changes the domain

graph_to_range.teacher_signal: Cannot express a graph's vertical outputs

domain_range_confusion.teacher_signal: Uses output behavior to restrict inputs

generalized_range.teacher_signal: Cannot generalize the range from parameters
